strengths: SLM Compression project (TinyLlama 1.1B, 8-bit quantization, ~55% VRAM reduction, <1% accuracy loss) is literally LLM inference optimization work — the closest direct backing for the JD line 'serve large language models efficiently.'

CUDA Kernel Optimization for VGG16 (custom coalesced kernels, 35% speedup over naive GPU, 1.5-2x over eager) and COFFIN capstone TensorRT-optimized YOLO (5.2x speedup) show genuine hands-on model-level performance engineering, matching 'high standard for performance' in About You.

MPI Hodgkin-Huxley and Parallel Ray Tracer projects (up to 30x speedup, SLURM-managed cluster) show real distributed/parallel computing instincts, though the domain is scientific/HPC computing rather than software infrastructure.
real_gaps: The role is platform engineering — building and maintaining shared internal tooling for a whole autonomy org (inference platform, compiler platform, workflow pipelines, observability). Every project in the profile is a single-person research or capstone build, not a multi-user internal platform used by other engineers.

No CI/CD, testing framework, or monitoring/observability stack anywhere in the profile — this directly maps to two of the five stated responsibilities ('continuous testing and monitoring,' 'observability... model lifecycle') with zero backing.
No ML workflow orchestration experience (Airflow, Kubeflow, Argo, MLflow, Metaflow) — explicitly a bonus point and the literal subject of the first responsibility bullet.
'ML compiler platform' implies building/maintaining compiler infrastructure (TVM/XLA/MLIR-style internals). Profile shows only consuming TensorRT and ONNX as an end user, not compiler-internals work.
overstated_by_keywords: 'distributed systems' was counted Adjacent by the keyword pass, but the actual experience (MPI/SLURM academic HPC clusters) is a different domain from the software-systems distributed infrastructure implied by an ML infra platform role.
'ML compiler' was counted as a preferred Have via TensorRT/ONNX familiarity — that is tool usage, not compiler platform engineering.
'ML pipelines' was counted Adjacent — the profile's pipelines are one-off training/inference scripts, not production workflow pipelines with validation gates before deployment.
llm_analysis.reasoning: Justin is genuinely strong on the narrow slice of this role that is single-model inference optimization (quantization, CUDA kernels, TensorRT), including real LLM-serving-adjacent work via the TinyLlama project. But roughly half the JD is platform/infra engineering scope (testing, monitoring, observability, workflow orchestration, compiler platform maintenance) with no direct evidence in the profile — those gaps are real, not just keyword misses, and the keyword pass's 100% match_pct meaningfully overstates fit for the role as actually scoped.
